name: Facet
text: Use Figma to build a clickable prototype of Excava’s interface. It lets users *feel* the navigation and interactions live, which beats static slides for clarity and enjoyment. The trade-off is time—Figma demands more upfront effort than Google Slides—but the payoff in liveliness and user testing speed justifies it.

name: Pane
text: Figma prototypes solve the liveliness problem but create a new risk: users mistake the polished demo for the real product, inflating expectations beyond what the backend can deliver. A better alternative is to pair a lightweight Figma clickable prototype—just enough to test navigation—with a live backend stub that returns real API responses but with fake data, so users see *interaction* without believing in *completeness*. Settle it by running a 15-minute user test: if users can’t distinguish the stub from the real thing, the prototype is too convincing.

name: Facet
text:
Build the Excava interface in Figma as a clickable prototype, then layer in a live backend demo only after navigation is locked. This keeps the prototype lean for quick iteration while avoiding the trap of overpromising on features before the core flow is solid. The trade-off is delaying the "wow" factor of a full live demo, but it prevents wasted effort on polished screens that might need scrapping later.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Figma’s polished demo still risks users conflating the prototype with the real product—even if navigation is locked. A better alternative is to pair a *rough* Figma wireframe (no polish) with a live backend demo from day one, forcing users to focus on function over form. Settle it with a user test: if users still mistake the wireframe for the real thing, the risk is real.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a rough Figma wireframe paired with a live backend demo from day one to force function-over-form focus, then polish navigation only after core flow is locked.

Result: A lean, user-tested interface skeleton with real backend interaction to set accurate expectations. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
